connectAiClient.title: Connect an AI client
connectAiClient.description: Let Claude Desktop, Cursor or another MCP client ask about your finances. It gets a read-only token of its own: it can read the same data you can see, including your private accounts, and it can never change anything.
connectAiClient.endpoint-hint: The client sends a personal API token with the mcp:read scope in an Authorization header. A browser session cookie is never accepted here.
connectAiClient.copy-failed: Could not copy. Select the text and copy it manually.
connectAiClient.totp-hint: Only needed if you use two-factor authentication.
connectAiClient.token-created-description: Copy it now and paste it into the client config below. It is stored only as a hash, so this is the only time it is shown.
connectAiClient.config-description: Paste the token where the example shows YOUR_TOKEN. The first block is for Claude Desktop, which bridges remote servers with mcp-remote; the second is the direct HTTP form used by Cursor and other clients.
connectAiClient.calls-description: Every tool an MCP client calls is recorded with its name and time. Amounts and descriptions are never written to the log.
connectAiClient.calls-empty: No AI client has called the server yet.
connectAiClient.error-create: Could not create the token. Try again.
connectAiClient.error-totp-required: Enter your authenticator code to create a token.
connectAiClient.error-invalid-totp: That authenticator code is not valid.
connectAiClient.error-session-not-fresh: Please sign in again before creating a token.
